### Considered and refused

- 2148 `ðā`: could be the relative 'which' (treasures, which I will bring) rather than the demonstrative; the semicolon at 2147 and `ðā` at the head of the unit favour the demonstrative, and l and i both give 'those/these'. Left; both readings give the same sense.
- 2145 `forloren hæfde` with dative `ðām lēanum`: forlēosan with a dative of what is lost is the construction I know from the glossary; not changed, but it is not checked against Klaeber's own glossary entry (not in the source file).
- 2149 `lissa`: i says 'happiness', l says 'favours'; the note already calls it a guess between two senses of `liss`. Left.
- 2152 `eafor, hēafodsegn` as two words: note already gives both readings. Left.
- 2158–2162 `Brūc ealles well!` kept as 'Make good use of it all!': a plain rendering of brūcan + genitive, not an echo of a known phrase.
- 2160 `nō ðȳ ǣr` 'none the sooner': checked against grammar (ðȳ instrumental); kept.
- 2166 `bregdon`: infinitive-vs-plural-subjunctive is already flagged as a guess in the note. Left.
- 2172 `ðēod(nes) dohtor` 'prince's daughter': i has 'a prince's daughter'; the OE gives no article. Left; the text does not say which prince, and the note does not guess.
- 2175 i drops `syððan`: 'after receiving the ring' already carries the sequence. Left.
- 2181 `hē mancynnes mǣste cræfte` kept as 'strongest of mankind': superlative with partitive genitive, no famous-translation echo.
- 2187 i 'firmly believed' for `swȳðe wēndon`: acceptable intensity; left.
- 2188 i 'an end to every one of his sorrows' for `torna gehwylces`: a free but sound rendering of the genitive; left.
- 2200 i 'it came about that … ' left as an unfinished frame because the sentence runs to 2207 and the unit cuts at a comma.
- 2204 `on sigeþēode` 'probably the Geats': already a stated guess.
- 2214 new `p` at 2214 (thief enters) refused: the dragon episode begins at 2210, which now has the paragraph break; 2214 continues it. New `p` at 2172 (second gift) refused: it continues the speech-aftermath paragraph; published parts break at new scenes, speech ends (19 of 23 times) and episodes, and 2163, 2177, 2190, 2200 already do. `p` NOT added at 2155 (speech start after a colon): published parts omit it 28 of 30 times.
- 2214–2220 restorations: not changed; see open uncertainty.
- Name forms in notes (Higelāc vs Hygelāc): normalised only in prose (2169, 2200, 2207); Old English quotations keep Klaeber's spelling.

### Open uncertainty (for QUESTIONS.md)

- 2212 `hēa(ụm) h(ǣþ)e`: restored text, Zupitza, Sedgefield, Chambers and Sievers disagree; the draft gives 'on the high heath' and says so.
- 2214–2220: the lost words (`(forþ nē)h gefe(al)g`, `hond (wǣge nam)`, `(sīd,)`, `(bemāð)`, `(onfand)`, `b(ig)folc`, `besyre(d wur)de`) are Klaeber's guesses against Bugge, Sedgefield and Trautmann; whether `nē hē þæt syððan (bemāð)` has the dragon or the thief as subject, and what `þæt` is, turns on them. The draft follows Klaeber and marks them as guesses.
- 2172 ring: Wealhtheow's ring (1192–1195) is said at 1202–1214 to have been Higelāc's and lost at his death; here Beowulf gives it to Hygd. The note now says how it came back is not told.
- 2183 `swā`: 'as' versus 'so that' chosen; either is defensible.

## Gloss check

Method: every gloss.json parse checked against the line (case, number, gender, tense, mood, lemma, meaning), for line numbers and 'here', for homograph handling, for damaged-text forms flagged as restorations, and against the notes in units.json. Every `__broaden__` entry verified by script: the old text equals the live entry in beowulf-glossary.json, whole, followed by ' · ' and one new reading. All 108 novel forms present, none redefined, none superfluous; no line numbers or 'here' in any entry; no entry over the 260-character limit.
